18. Secondly, Mr. Mahbubuddin has argued that the non-production of the original F.I.R receipts and other material papers and non-examination of Sk. Abdullah, Magistrate, 1st class, who led the trap raise serious doubt as to the truth of the prosecution case and in view of these lapses a  presumption adverse to the prosecution should be drawn. It has already been noticed that some of the original papers namely, the F.I.R. and a seizure-list are not on the record but there are carbon copies. It is found from the evidence of P.W. 11, Habibur Rahman, A.S.I., that the original F.I.R. was lost from the Martial Law office and the other papers were lost from the Malkhana. From. Ext. 25 it appears that in the later part of 1971 the records of this case were called for by the Military authorities and Ext 27 shows that all the papers including the missing ones were received at the Malkhana on 5-9-72. A pre-prosperous suggestion was put to the I/O that he had himself destroyed the papers. Since the original papers were proved to have been lost there was no bar in law in proving those documents by secondary evidence. As to the missing stamped receipts an d the pages of Ext. 13, I am of the view that since the prosecution case is based upon actual recovery of Tk. 2000/- from the appellant, those papers were not very material but would have only helped in strengthening the prosecution case. Mr. Mahbubuddin having realized the position has not pressed further on the ground of documents but insisted that the examination of the Magistrate was very much necessary to prove the alleged occurrence of recovery of Tk. 2000/- from the person of appellant. 

 19. I entirely agree with the learned advocate for the appellant that the Magistrate was a very material 'witness for the prosecution to prove this case beyond all reasonable doubt and ordinarily the non-examination of such witnesses must affect the prosecution case very adversely. Let me, however, examine as to whether the prosecution was diligent enough to examine such a material witness. It is found from the order of the Special Judge that the Magistrate concerned was posted at Zakiganj, Sylhet and several adjournments were taken for this or that difficulty of the Magistrate. He was to depose before the Special Judge on 14-11-73 but on his way to Jessore he fell ill at Dacca and sent a telegraph accordingly. On that occasion the learned Special Judge granted time on the prayer of the prosecution and without issuing a warrant of arrest against the Magistrate thought it proper to ask the District Magistrate, Sylhet to send the Magistrate concerned on the next date of hearing i.e. 16-2-74. It appears from the record that a radiogram was sent from the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet addressed to the Deputy Commissioner, Jessore informing that Mr. Sk. Abdullah, Magistrate could not be spared to depose on 18-2-74 as he was engaged in food procurement drive and it was advised to pray for sufficient time. The A.P.P. filed a petition for adjournment of the case on the basis of the aforesaid radiogram which is on record. The learned Special Judge, however, by order dated 18-2-74 rejected the prayer for time observing that enough time since 26-2-73 involving several adjournments were already granted for the production of the witness. It is true that the court could not indefinitely wait for a witness to appear and depose in the case but from the facts on record I find that the prosecution cannot be said to have been indolent in the matter or to have withheld the witness purposely, but for some reason or other which were beyond the control of the prosecution the Magistrate could not ultimately be produced before the court. In such circumstances I do not think it proper to draw any presumption adverse to the prosecution for it did not willfully withhold the Magistrate from the court. The opinion that the prosecution case for whatever it is worth must be considered on the basis of the evidence which is already on record. The non-examination of the Magistrate has certainly weakened the prosecution case but it remains to be seen as to whether upon the evidence on record the prosecution case can yet be said to have been established beyond reasonable doubt.
